en.headline: Two projector stands removed from Peak lighting project after outcry
en.dek: Commissioner for Tourism Ann Chan inspected the Lugard Road site Saturday morning, and the metal stands that held industrial projectors were gone by afternoon, leaving only their foundations.
body: The Hong Kong Tourism Board has removed two large metal stands that held industrial-grade projectors as part of a lighting installation along the Lugard Road and Harlech Road walking trail on The Peak.

The South China Morning Post reported that the removals followed an inspection of the site on Saturday morning by Commissioner for Tourism Ann Chan Wai-yan, together with a lawmaker and a district councillor. Residents had previously accused the board of removing trees and flowers to make way for the installations.

A security guard near the park on the circular walk told the newspaper that the two structures were taken down that afternoon. When the paper visited late on Saturday afternoon, only the grey foundational blocks and some bolts remained, and they were not cordoned off.

Authorities have said the project is not set in stone and that a revised proposal will be submitted to the Central and Western District Council next month for consultation. The lighting trail was intended as part of a new themed light show under Hong Kong WinterFest to replace the long-running Symphony of Lights.

zh.headline: 山頂光影項目兩座投影機支架已拆除 居民早前反對
zh.dek: 旅遊事務專員陳慧茜周六早上視察盧吉道及夏力道一帶，下午大型金屬支架已被移除，只剩地基。
body: 香港旅遊發展局已拆除山頂盧吉道及夏力道步行徑光影裝置中兩座承載工業級投影機的大型金屬支架。
南華早報報道，拆除行動在周六早上旅遊事務專員陳慧茜聯同立法會議員及區議員視察現場後不久進行。居民早前批評旅發局為安裝設施而移除樹木及花卉。
一名靠近公園的保安員向報章表示，兩座支架於當天下午被拆走。報章下午稍後到訪時，現場只剩灰色地基及螺栓，並未圍封。
當局此前表示項目並非一成不變，並將於下月向中西區區議會提交修訂方案作諮詢。該光影步道原計劃配合香港冬季節慶活動，取代長年的幻彩詠香江燈光秀。
